chapter: Instruments, tenors and the current band
title: Buying the engraved alto from Sam Marowitz around 1944-46
summary: Herman bought the alto, found by Sam Marowitz in a New York pawn shop, around 1944-46 when an alto player left, and uses it for ballads.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone

blocks.x: -- just mention about the alto [Wang,] did you say, or -- you used a word. What did you call that alto?
Well, I don't know what I just said.
I don't know, you just said something --
It's a very engraved varying degree kind of instrument.
Yeah.
Did that have anything to do with it, as far as I knew?
Uh-huh.
There was only two models, or two particular saxophones built like this by Selmer Sumner.
Oh, I see.
And one --
Yeah.
-- wound up in the hands of the fellow I said.
How did you acquire this, now? Did they send it to you?
Oh, no, I bought it through a very dear friend of mine, Sam Merowitz. He found it in a hock shop in New York.
He did?
Of course. Is there a better way to --
Yeah, that's the best way to find it.
And that's a bad expression. So I'll put it this way, in the words of Sam Merowitz. It was a He would say "repair shop."
Very good.

When did you pick that up?
About 1945, '46. Between '45 and '46.
I see.
Maybe even earlier, '44, because it was when some alto player split and I decided to take over.
Oh, I see. You use that -- you use it with a lot of nice ballad things that I've through the years heard you use it quite often with that.
That's the only groove I've ever been into. (Inaudible).
